Visit note | 2025-10-16 02:30 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Fariha Alam, 31, female. Mrs. Alam reports that she has been suffering from bothersome wheezing and coughing at night. She mentions that these respiratory symptoms have become notably worse since construction dust started near her home in Jashore. She works as a ride-share driver and has a medical history significant for Type 2 diabetes mellitus. During the consultation, she denies any chest pain or fever. On examination: SpO2 93%, BP 121/81 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 81 kg. Auscultation reveals bilateral expiratory wheezes; her heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued today. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and carefully learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-10-16 03:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Jewel Molla, 47, male. Mr. Molla presents with troubling night pain in the shoulder, being unable to raise his arm properly, and a stiff shoulder that has persisted for weeks. He explains that his shoulder discomfort began gradually after a long illness in Khulna. He earns his living as an office cleaner and reports no prior chronic medical conditions. He denies any recent trauma, neck pain, or numbness down the arm. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 100 degrees, BP 113/85 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 80 kg. Joint tenderness is noted around the capsule with restricted passive and active range of motion. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to start physiotherapy, perform pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-10-16 03:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Fatema Hossain, 38, female. Mrs. Hossain attends for a follow-up review regarding her recurrent episodes of breathlessness during attacks, normal heart tests, and an overwhelming fear of dying. She notes that these distressing panic attacks began after a traffic accident in Mohammadpur. She works as a lawyer and has no known comorbidities. She reports experiencing about 3 panic attacks in the last month. On examination: BP 117/71 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 58 kg. She was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine intake, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-10-18 11:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Salma Bepari, 75, female. Mrs. Bepari comes in today for a scheduled follow-up evaluation regarding recurrent episodes of fluttering in her chest accompanied by intermittent dizzy spells. She mentions that these distressing symptoms were first noticed while resting quietly after a family lunch at her residence in Bashundhara. She works as a homemaker and reports no prior history of chronic systemic illnesses or major surgeries. She denies any previous episodes of chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or sudden fainting spells, though she admits to feeling fatigued easily over the past few weeks. On clinical examination today, her pulse is irregular at 134 beats per minute, blood pressure is recorded at 126/77 mmHg, and her weight is 90 kg. Cardiovascular examination reveals an irregularly irregular heart rhythm with varying pulse volumes, but no audible murmurs or gallops. Respiratory examination shows clear lung fields bilaterally with no basal crepitus or wheezing, and her peripheral perfusion is adequate with no lower limb edema. Following a comprehensive review of her clinical presentation and recent rhythm strips, the doctor establishes the diagnosis of Atrial fibrillation. A formal management plan is outlined, and it is noted that a prescription was issued to help control her heart rate and mitigate thromboembolic risks. She receives detailed lifestyle guidance, including instructions to limit tea and coffee intake, completely avoid alcohol consumption, and report any fainting or worsening dizziness at once. Her follow-up is scheduled in 2 weeks with a repeat ECG and essential kidney function tests to monitor her ongoing treatment safely.
